entities.name: Ralph
entities.subtype: youngest son of King Peter of Upmeads; questing knight
entities.summary: Quester for the Well at the World's End; wintered with Ursula in the rock-house in the Valley of Sweet-chestnuts; slays a great bear and weds Ursula there.

attributes.status_in_batch: weds Ursula (BTHREE-C14); drinks of the Well (BTHREE-C21)

refs.q: who thrust the beast into the side with his long-headed spear
This maiden, who is my fellow-farer in the Quest, I desire to wed this same night

entities.name: Ursula
entities.subtype: maiden of Upmeads; Ralph's fellow-farer, later wife
entities.summary: Ralph's companion on the Quest; carries sword and a little axe; weds Ralph before the messengers of the Innocent Folk.

refs.q: Ralph saw that she had a little axe in her hand
bade him and the young men bear witness that they were wedded

entities.name: (unnamed) rock-house in the Valley of Sweet-chestnuts
entities.subtype: cave dwelling with a toft before it
entities.summary: The cave/rock-house where Ralph and Ursula wintered; a little quicken-tree grows by the door; a grassy toft before it where they cook; the Innocent Folk's messengers come to this cave every spring.

refs.q: Ralph sat alone on the toft by the rock-house
which grew hard by the door
who come every spring to this cave to see if there be any whom they may speed

entities.name: Valley of Sweet-chestnuts
entities.subtype: mountain valley with meadow, chestnut grove and river
entities.summary: Valley where Ralph and Ursula wintered; meadows, a chestnut grove between the rock-house and the river, bears frequent the meadows in spring.

refs.q: when they were gone eight days from the Valley of Sweet-chestnuts

entities.name: (unnamed) river of the Valley of Sweet-chestnuts
entities.summary: River below the meadow of the rock-house where Ursula bathes; green grass runs down to the water's edge beyond the chestnut grove.

refs.q: Ursula had gone down the meadow to disport her and to bathe in the river

entities.name: (unnamed) chestnut grove
entities.summary: Grove of chestnuts between the rock-house and the river; the bridal bower was built in it; the bear's skin and carcase hung on a tree there.

refs.q: Now there was a grove of chestnuts betwixt him and the river
they all went down the meadow together into the chestnut grove

entities.name: (unnamed) sandy bight under the mountains
entities.summary: Place under the mountains where Ralph and Ursula saw a family of bears the day before the bear attack.

refs.q: they had come across a family of the beasts in the sandy bight under the mountains

entities.name: bear (of the wastes)
entities.summary: Bears haunt the meadows in spring; fierce and proud in the wastes; the he-bear slain by Ralph was as big as a bullock and fought rearing like a boxer.

refs.q: with the waxing spring the bears were often in the meadows again
held in chase by a huge bear as big as a bullock
having risen to his hind legs, fenced with his great paws like a boxer

entities.name: quicken-tree
entities.summary: A little quicken-tree grows hard by the door of the rock-house; Ursula's sword hung on its bough.

refs.q: hanging to a bough of a little quicken-tree, which grew hard by the door

entities.name: Ralph's spear
entities.subtype: spear made from dagger blade and ashen shaft
entities.summary: Ralph fits a dagger blade to a long ashen shaft to make a strong spear against bears.

refs.q: Ralph was fitting the blade of a dagger to a long ashen shaft, to make him a strong spear

entities.name: Ursula's helm and hauberk
entities.summary: Armour kept in the cave which Ralph puts on Ursula while he skins the bear.

refs.q: to don thine helm and hauberk to boot
brought forth the armour and did it on her

entities.name: Bourton Abbas
entities.summary: Recalled as where Ursula seemed to weep for her betrothed at the ale-house.

refs.q: at the ale-house at Bourton Abbas

entities.name: (unnamed) ale-house at Bourton Abbas
entities.summary: Ale-house at Bourton Abbas where Ralph first saw Ursula (recalled).

refs.q: for whom thou wepst or seemedst to weep at the ale-house at Bourton Abbas

entities.name: Upmeads
entities.summary: Ralph proposes to go back with Ursula to Upmeads straightway; Ursula says the homeward road's perils would overcome them without the Well's water.

refs.q: I am minded to go back with thee to Upmeads straightway

entities.name: Well at the World's End
entities.summary: Goal of the Quest; drinking from it is held needful to survive the perils of the homeward road.

refs.q: if we have not drunk of the Well at the World's End

entities.name: Innocent Folk
entities.summary: A gentle, reverent folk who send messengers every spring to the cave to speed seekers of the Well; brown-skinned, clad in white wool; dwell in an unfenced town with a Temple/Mote-house/Guest-house; keep a behest to the fairest woman of the world.

refs.q: those messengers of the Innocent Folk, who come every spring to this cave
somewhat brown of skin, but well fashioned, and of smiling cheerful countenance
On the evening of that day they came into the town of that folk

entities.name: Messengers of the Innocent Folk
entities.summary: Two young men and an elder with five oxen (three for riding, two sumpter), clad in white wool, no armour, each with a green-stone axe; the young men carry bows; they lead seekers as far as the House of the Sorceress.

refs.q: he found there two young men and an elder, and they had with them five oxen
to be your way-leaders as far as the House of the Sorceress

entities.name: (unnamed) elder of the Innocent Folk (messenger)
entities.summary: Elder with a long white beard, bright eye, firm smooth hand; once in his youth led a mounted knight to the Well; witnesses Ralph and Ursula's wedding.

refs.q: The elder had a long white beard, but his eye was bright
once in his young days he had led a man to the Well who was riding a horse

entities.name: (unnamed) two young men of the Innocent Folk
entities.summary: The elder's 'sons' (as he calls them); carry strong bows and quivers; build the bridal bower; marvel at horses.

refs.q: Up, my sons, and show your deftness to these dear friends!

entities.name: green-stone axe
entities.summary: Each messenger bears an axe with a green stone blade curiously tied to the heft.

refs.q: each had an axe with a green stone blade, curiously tied to the heft

entities.name: ox (riding and sumpter)
entities.subtype: oxen as mounts and pack beasts
entities.summary: The Innocent Folk ride oxen and use them as pack beasts; slow-going; hobbled at rest.

refs.q: five oxen, three for riding, and two sumpter beasts, laden
for oxen are but slow-going nags

entities.name: pair of beads (token of the Well)
entities.summary: The pair of beads borne by each seeker is a token of the Quest whose fashion the Innocent Folk know.

refs.q: the pair of beads which we bear, either of us, and the fashion whereof ye know

entities.name: House of the Sorceress
entities.summary: Destination to which the messengers lead seekers, where they get other help.

refs.q: to be your way-leaders as far as the House of the Sorceress, where ye shall have other help

entities.name: fairest woman of the world (Lady of Abundance)
entities.summary: The Innocent Folk come yearly by behest made to 'the fairest woman of the world' when she came back from the Well; CANON-INFERRED identity with the Lady of Abundance from earlier books.

refs.q: according to the behest that we made to the fairest woman of the world

entities.name: (unnamed) bridal bower
entities.summary: Wattled bower of willow boughs and stakes built in the chestnut grove, roofed with skins, hung with garlands, floor strewn with flowers, as the Innocent Folk build for their own wedding nights.

refs.q: they had made a very goodly wattled bower, and roofed it with the skins that were in the cave

entities.name: (unnamed) shepherds of the Innocent Folk
entities.summary: Four folk (two carles, two queans) shepherding uncouth-looking sheep on a green hill-side; ruder of raiment than the way-leaders.

refs.q: four folk shepherding them, two carles to wit, and two queans

entities.name: (unnamed) wide valley of the Innocent Folk
entities.summary: Wide, well-grassed and watered valley, wooded here and there, with scattered cots, garths of young corn and vineyards on the hillsides.

refs.q: came into a wide valley, well-grassed and watered, and wooded here and there

entities.name: (unnamed) town of the Innocent Folk
entities.summary: Simple town wholly unfenced for war, with low small houses; no filth, famine or poverty.

refs.q: which was but simple, wholly unfenced for war, and the houses but low, and not great

entities.name: Temple / Mote-house / Guest-house of the Innocent Folk
entities.subtype: temple, moot-house and guest-house in one
entities.summary: A great and fair house in the town that serves as temple, mote-house and guest-house; has a hall with a dais and chambers.

refs.q: up to the door of the Temple, or Mote-house, or Guest-house, for it was all these

entities.name: Elders of the Innocent Folk
entities.summary: Elders stand before the Mote-house to receive seekers; the eldest greets them.

refs.q: Before the door thereof were standing the elders of the Folk

entities.name: (unnamed) eldest elder of the Innocent Folk
entities.summary: Greets the seekers 'after length of days and happy times'.

refs.q: Welcome and thrice welcome to the Seekers after length of days and happy times

entities.name: white woollen cloth / frieze
entities.summary: The Innocent Folk dress in white woollen cloth or frieze; fine white wool raiment embroidered with bright bird feathers given to the couple.

refs.q: clad goodly after their fashion in white woollen cloth or frieze
broidered in strange but beauteous fashion with the feathers of bright-hued birds

entities.name: Wedding custom of witnesses

such kissing and caressing as is meet betwixt troth-plight lovers

facts.subject: bears
facts.statement: In spring bears return to the meadows; a family of bears (carle, quean and cubs) seen; bears fierce and proud in the wastes and intolerant of other creatures, but they avoided two armed men in sunlight.

refs.q: although they were fierce and proud in those wastes, and could not away with creatures that were not of their kind

facts.subject: Ralph
facts.statement: Ralph slays the bear with a spear thrust to the side, cuts off a fore-paw, and drives his sword over the shoulder to the heart.

refs.q: drave the sword in over the shoulder so happily that it reached his heart

facts.subject: Ralph and Ursula
facts.statement: They cook meat (venison) at a fire on the toft before the cave; Ursula 'dights victual'; Ralph skins and breaks up the bear and hangs skin and carcase on a tree.

refs.q: there was already venison roasting at the fire on the toft
Then he hung the skin and the carcase on a tree of the grove

facts.subject: Valley of Sweet-chestnuts
facts.statement: Spring in the valley: birdsong, scent of blossoms on the west wind.

refs.q: the scent of many blossoms went past on the wings of the west wind

facts.subject: marriage
facts.statement: Ursula recalls that since heathen days weddings were witnessed by the whole folk; the couple wait for the Innocent Folk to be witnesses besides God.

refs.q: while our people were yet heathen, when a man should wed a maid all the folk knew of it

facts.subject: Well at the World's End
facts.statement: Ursula holds that the perils of the homeward road will overcome them unless they have drunk of the Well.

refs.q: the perils of the homeward road shall overcome us, despite of love

facts.subject: Innocent Folk
facts.statement: The messengers come every spring to the cave; it is many a year since they last found seekers there; the elder once led a horse-riding knight to the Well in his youth.

refs.q: it is many and many a year ago since we found any seekers after the Well dwelling here
led a man to the Well who was riding a horse and was clad in knightly array

facts.subject: Innocent Folk
facts.statement: The Innocent Folk had never seen horses (the young men), riding oxen and using oxen as pack beasts; the sheep-folk also marvelled at horses and weapons.

refs.q: Their horses and all their gear were a great wonder to the young men, for they had seen no such beasts before
they marvelled exceedingly at their horses and weapons

facts.subject: Innocent Folk
facts.statement: Messengers bear no armour; green-stone bladed axes; young men carry strong bows and quivers.

refs.q: bore no armour, but each had an axe with a green stone blade

facts.subject: Innocent Folk
facts.statement: The messengers bring raiment, meal and wine on sumpter-beasts; wine in well-hooped kegs, carved wooden cups; the elder bakes cakes from meal at the fire.

refs.q: there was wine there in well-hooped kegs, and wooden cups fairly carven
had taken meal thence, and was making cakes at the fire

facts.subject: Innocent Folk
facts.statement: For their own weddings the Innocent Folk build a bower in which the couple spend the wedding night.

refs.q: such a bower as we build for our own folk on the night of the wedding

facts.subject: bridal bower
facts.statement: Built of cut willow boughs, driven stakes and woven twigs (wattle), roofed with skins, garlanded, floor strewn with flowers.

refs.q: cut willow boughs, and such-like wood, and drave stakes and wove the twigs together

facts.subject: Innocent Folk
facts.statement: Wedding raiment of fine white wool embroidered with feathers of bright-hued birds.

refs.q: raiment of fine white wool for those twain, broidered in strange but beauteous fashion

facts.subject: marriage
facts.statement: The wedding is made by the couple standing before the elder at moonlit night after a feast and bidding the witnesses bear witness; no priest.

refs.q: they stood before the elder, and bade him and the young men bear witness that they were wedded

facts.subject: Ralph
facts.statement: Ralph asks whether wedding and carnal knowledge would hurt the Quest; the elder says they hear not that it shall be worse.

refs.q: we hear not that it shall be the worse for you in any wise that ye shall become one flesh

facts.subject: Innocent Folk
facts.statement: Their land has sheep and neat in plenty, garths of young corn, and vineyards on hillsides; cots scattered in the valley; sheep described as uncouth-looking.

refs.q: they passed by garths wherein the young corn was waxing, and vineyards on the hillsides

facts.subject: Innocent Folk
facts.statement: The folk are kind but over-reverent, greeting with more worship than fellowship; no filth, famine, poverty or misery; town unfenced for war.

refs.q: These men greeted them kindly, and yet with more worship than fellowship

facts.subject: Innocent Folk
facts.statement: Runners go ahead to announce arrivals; townsfolk line the way with bowed heads; seekers are bathed, clad in fine fragrant white gowns, crowned with flowers and set on a dais like kings or gods; feast with songs by youths and maidens.

refs.q: for runners had gone before them
they set them down on a dais as though they had been kings, or rather gods

facts.subject: Innocent Folk
facts.statement: A single great house serves as Temple, Mote-house and Guest-house.

refs.q: the Temple, or Mote-house, or Guest-house, for it was all these

facts.subject: Innocent Folk
facts.statement: Their songs are simple and harmless, about the fairness of the earth and the happy loves of creatures.

refs.q: concerning the fairness of the earth and the happy loves of the creatures that dwell therein

ledger.summary: In spring in the Valley of Sweet-chestnuts Ralph kills a huge bear that chased Ursula after she bathed in the river. They declare their love; Ursula wishes to wait for the yearly messengers of the Innocent Folk as wedding witnesses. Ralph skins the bear.
ledger.geography_notes: Rock-house with toft and quicken-tree; chestnut grove between it and the river; meadow sloping to river; sandy bight under the mountains; bear carcase two furlongs from the dwelling.
open_questions: Exact layout of the valley relative to the mountains.

ledger.summary: Messengers of the Innocent Folk (an elder and two young men with oxen) arrive and offer to guide them to the House of the Sorceress. They build a wattled bower in the chestnut grove and witness Ralph and Ursula's wedding that night.
ledger.geography_notes: Bower in chestnut grove; messengers come yearly to the cave.

ledger.summary: Travelling with the messengers, the couple leave the mountains in three days, see them as a cloud after six, meet shepherds on day eight and on day nine enter a settled valley and the unfenced town of the Innocent Folk, where they are feasted in the Temple/Mote-house/Guest-house.
ledger.geography_notes: Route: Valley of Sweet-chestnuts -> out of mountains (3 days) -> mountains a cloud behind (6 days) -> sheep on green hillside (8 days) -> wide valley and town (9th day). No compass direction given.
open_questions: Direction from the mountains to the Innocent Folk.
